nonblocking_findings: F32 [Nit] review-b: run-g6-mutant.sh edits the tracked file dashboard/lib/document-wrapper/chibi-quest-styles.ts in place and restores it from an untracked backup. Rationale: the script does not make the backup /tmp/opencode/g6-chibi-styles-backup.ts, and no committed record says how to make it (run-g6-mutant.sh:6, :12, :36). The script prints before_sha256 and backup_sha256 but does not compare them. A stale backup would revert a later product change without a signal. The script has no trap. It applies the mutant (lines 15-25) before it calls heavy-run.sh. That wrapper can wait for the shared lock and the memory pre-flight (HEAVY_PREFLIGHT_WAIT_S=5400 at line 30). Other agents in the checkout can read the mutated file during that wait. The last command is echo G6_DONE (line 40), so the exit code is always 0. Hence rerun-gates.sh:19-20 and green-s5g8-g6-rerun.txt (G6_RERUN_EXIT=0) cannot show a surviving mutant or a failed restore. No harm occurred at HEAD. The file hash equals before_sha256 and restored_sha256 in green-s5g8-g6.txt. That file also shows MUTANT_TEST_EXIT=1 and RESTORE_DIFF_EXIT=0. The product folders match HEAD. Suggested fix for the next Green round: compare the two hashes and stop when they differ. Restore from git in a trap. Apply the mutant inside the heavy-run command. Exit 1 when the mutant survives or the restore differs.

Suggested fix: restore that file from HEAD before the next commit. Make S5_ROUND required, or refuse to write over a tracked file.
